findings.evidence: U1 publishes the dev database on 127.0.0.1:${JADE_DEV_DB_PORT:-5432}, and V5 makes env:init choose 5432 whenever it is free. pnpm test needs that database (U7 integration harness), and section 16 step 3 runs pnpm test and then pnpm test:infra in the same gate. pnpm ci:local runs ci:check (database up) before ci:image and test:infra. So when compose-up.test.ts probes host port 5432, the dev Postgres answers and the test fails, even though the stack's db publishes nothing. AC8 then cannot pass locally, and an implementer may be pushed to weaken the check.
findings.fix: Assert exposure from the stack itself, not from a host port that other things may hold. Use `docker compose -p <test project> ps --format json` or `docker inspect` to require that the app and db containers have no Publishers or PortBindings. If a connection probe is kept, aim it at the stack containers' own addresses, or at a port the test has just checked is unused on the host.
findings.path: plan section 11, Checks, tests/infra/compose-up.test.ts ('ports 3000 and 5432 refuse connections from the host'); section 9 U1; section 16 step 3; section 12.1 X1 (ci:local)

findings.evidence: migrate() takes a session advisory lock and then calls ensureAppRole(), which sets jade_app's password from a SCRAM verifier computed in the tool. Each verifier has a fresh salt, so the role row is rewritten on every run. Postgres advisory locks are scoped to the current database, but pg_authid is shared across the cluster. Vitest runs files in parallel (U7), and migrate.test.ts and db-scripts.test.ts both run migrate() against their own fresh or scratch databases. Two ALTER ROLE jade_app statements can therefore run at the same time, and the second fails with 'ERROR: tuple concurrently updated' (CatalogTupleUpdate on a concurrently updated tuple). The result is intermittent integration failures, locally and in CI job check. The plan's 'two runners cannot interleave' guarantee only holds within one database.
findings.fix: Serialize role setup across the whole cluster, for example by taking the advisory lock in a fixed maintenance database (postgres) around ensureAppRole, or by running role DDL under a lock held across databases. Alternatively, alter the role only when it is missing or when logging in with the URL's password fails, and do the role bootstrap once in the integration global setup. Add a check that starts migrate() on two different databases at once and requires both to succeed.
findings.path: plan section 9 U2 (ensureAppRole), U3 steps 1-2 (advisory lock), U7, Checks (migrate.test.ts, db-scripts.test.ts)

findings.evidence: INV1 and CLAUDE.md rule 4 (OB41: plain kit codes, join codes and tokens are never logged) have no environment exception. A1 adds one: under APP_ENV=development the raw error, message included, is printed. /dev/boom is built to put the request's query string into that message, and later routes will see the same path, for example a code in /redeem?code= or a route parameter. D3 brings up the local production stack with the .env from pnpm env:init, which is the development .env (APP_ENV=development). The app container's stdout and stderr go to Docker's json-file logs on disk, so raw error text holding codes is stored. log-privacy.test.ts runs the built server under APP_ENV=test, so it never exercises this path. The brief forbids relaxing rules 1 to 6, and section 16 sends any change touching the logger's contract to Mike.
findings.fix: Remove the raw-error print, or limit it to the same fields as the JSON error line (type, tag, stack frames). If a fuller development view is wanted, make it an explicit opt-in that never applies under compose.prod.yml, and raise it to Mike as a rule-4 question. Run log-privacy.test.ts under APP_ENV=development as well as test, and have the local production stack use APP_ENV=production or staging rather than the development .env value.
findings.path: plan section 10 A1 ('In APP_ENV=development only, the raw error is also printed to the terminal'); A5 (/dev/boom puts the query string in the message); section 5 INV1; section 11 D3 (local compose.prod.yml uses the env:init .env)

findings.evidence: V6 says the tools call tools/load-env.ts, and pnpm db:migrate needs .env locally, so tools/db/migrate.ts imports ../load-env.ts. D1 copies tools/db/ into the runtime image but not tools/load-env.ts. In the image, `node tools/db/migrate.ts` would then fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, the migrate service would exit non-zero, and the app would never start. compose-up.test.ts would catch this, but the plan's file list is wrong.
findings.fix: List tools/load-env.ts (or all of tools/ that the migration entry point imports) in D1's runtime copy, or keep the migration entry point free of the loader in the image. Have image.test.ts run the migration entry point inside the image.
findings.path: plan section 11 D1 (runtime stage copies tools/db/ only); section 8 V6 (the tools call tools/load-env.ts)

findings.evidence: The single .env that D3 uses for compose.prod.yml is the development .env. Its DATABASE_URL and MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL point at 127.0.0.1:<dev port> (V5). If compose.prod.yml passes those through, migrate and app connect to 127.0.0.1 inside their containers and fail, so OB13 fails. The remark that generated passwords 'can sit in a URL unescaped' suggests the URLs are built in the Compose file from password variables. But no app-role password variable is named (only JADE_OWNER_DB_PASSWORD), and the plan does not say how the URLs are built.
findings.fix: State that compose.prod.yml builds both URLs with host db, for example postgres://jade_app:${JADE_APP_DB_PASSWORD:?}@db:5432/jade. Add JADE_APP_DB_PASSWORD to .env.example and env:init, keep the dev DATABASE_URL consistent with it, and have compose-config.test.ts assert the host is db.
findings.path: plan section 11 D2 (app 'receives DATABASE_URL (app role)', migrate 'receives both URLs'); section 8 V5; section 11 D3

findings.evidence: Compose gives COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME and -p precedence over a top-level name:. The bugfix skill exports COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=bugfix-<bead>-<purpose> for every gate. In that shell, compose.dev.yml and compose.prod.yml land in one project, each with a service called db, so a manual compose.prod.yml up would recreate the dev db container with the production configuration. The infra tests pass their own -p, so they are safe, but the plan's 'never touches' claim is false. Two checkouts also share the jade-stack name.
findings.fix: Qualify the claim, give the production stack distinct service and volume names or always use an explicit -p, and mention the interaction in the U8 edit to the bugfix skill.
findings.path: plan section 11 D2 ('name: jade-stack ... bringing it up in a checkout never touches the development db service'); .claude/skills/bugfix/SKILL.md 'The gates' (COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME)

findings.evidence: The image job runs pnpm ci:image and pnpm test:infra, which is Vitest, so it needs pnpm install. The other jobs allow 1:15 cold for setup and install. With the same allowance the image job is about 6:00 cold, not 5:15, which narrows the stated slack. It is still under the 9-minute timeout.
findings.fix: Budget setup and install for the image job the same way as the other jobs, and restate the whole-run estimate.
